body: Quick pass: merges cleanly with main; text only (AGENTS.md, README, three skills, a decision file with the migration script, PROCESS_VERSION 27); no label or issue was changed by it. Flagged ready for a read review; it changes the Issue Law, so it merges only on the maintainer's yes, and the relabel script runs once right after.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 5c8c32dc26be176d7ae12dc91ea3f41d7bc66cc9 -->
**Read, not built: text only.** Needs changes before merge. This is a law change, so it merges only on the maintainer's yes.

Read at head `5c8c32dc` against main `0fc30b65`, with issue #1189 and its comments. Nothing was built; no label or issue was touched by the PR (checked). `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` 26 -> 27, `Changelog: none`, `Fixes #1189`: all fine.

### What looks good
- The "Priorities" table (AGENTS.md:98-108) matches the issue's table level by level, in both what each level means and what it "was". The examples column was dropped, which is fine.
- The filing rules (AGENTS.md:110-119) match the issue: `P1`-`P3` are for defects only; `P4` only with the maintainer's words quoted; a follow-up is `P7` unless it is a defect; never `P?`.
- These are updated correctly: Pick (lowest number, then oldest; the search still has `-label:"P?"`), the enhancement-lane order, the safety floor (AGENTS.md:273, classify-effort:66), the red-gate filing (`P1`/`P2`, AGENTS.md:788-789), and the `P?` law (unchanged apart from the numbers).
- A grep over `AGENTS.md .claude README.md .github` at the head finds no `P0` left outside the "Was" column and the quoted words, and no untouched sentence that uses `P1`/`P2` in the old sense.
- The three eval files of each gh-issues eval agree with each other (P7 follow-up; lowest-number-first pick). In jq, `PZ` sorts after `P9` (string compare, `Z` > `9`), so the skill's default is right where it was changed.

### Blockers

**1. The two cut rules can be read against each other, and the decision file contradicts the maintainer.** AGENTS.md:111-113 says "Only `P1` and `P2` hold a release cut back" and cites the maintainer ("only P1 and P2 block a release cut"). That reads as: any open `P1`/`P2` blocks. AGENTS.md:791-792 says a cut does not start "while a `P1` or `P2` **it opened** is unfixed", which is only the gate's own issues. On top of that, `docs/decisions/1189-p1-p9-scale.md:24-25` lists "Widening the cut blocker to 'any open `P1`/`P2`'" as *considered and dropped*, and line 13 says "`P1` or `P2` the gate opened". The maintainer's choice in the #1189 comment is the wide one. Proposed:
- AGENTS.md:791-792: "...the issue is worked in the normal order, and a minor/major cut does not start while any `P1` or `P2` is open ("Priorities"); a `P3` never holds one."
- Decision file: line 13 becomes "cut blocker (any open `P1` or `P2`; a `P3` never)". Delete the "Widening the cut blocker" bullet at 24-25, or move it under "Chosen". If the narrower reading was in fact intended, the maintainer has to say so, and AGENTS.md:111 must then say "only a `P1` or `P2` the red gate opened".

**2. The MCP rule overrides the defect table.** AGENTS.md:512 says "Every MCP issue ... carries `area:mcp` and is `P5`". Under the new table, a defect in `crates/app/src/mcp/` (an MCP tool that posts wrong G-code, crashes, or refuses a legal input) is `P1`-`P3`. The two sentences contradict each other, and the MCP one is the more specific, so it wins. Under the old scale there was no conflict, because MCP was already the top non-safety level. Proposed (AGENTS.md:511-513): "Every MCP issue (...) carries `area:mcp` and is at least `P5` - a defect in it takes `P1`-`P3` by the "Priorities" table - unless the maintainer paused it `P?` (...)". camcraft-mcp SKILL.md:146 and :153 are fine as they are: they cover the `MCP: <command>` missing-tool follow-up, which is `P5`.

**3. A human-filed issue with no priority has no rule, and the skill sorts it after `P9`.** AGENTS.md:263-265 gives the triage rule for the *effort* label only. Nothing assigns a priority to a human-filed issue that arrives without one. The Pick snippet sorts it as `PZ`, behind "someday". Today that applies to #266 ("Gouge check sweeps a tap at its full diameter", open, human-filed, no `P*`) and about 18 others. A user-reported gouge-check bug would be picked last, which contradicts "User-reported bugs outrank owed work". Proposed, as a new bullet under "Priorities" after AGENTS.md:119: "A human-filed issue without a priority gets one at triage, by this table, from the first agent that reads it for a pick (with its effort label); it is ranked only once it has one."

**4. The two copies of the gh-issues Pick snippet disagree.** `.claude/skills/gh-issues/references/claim-workflow.md:28` still has `first // "P9"`, while `SKILL.md:55` was changed to `// "PZ"`. With `P9`, an unlabelled issue ties with `P9` and sorts by age among them. Also, claim-workflow.md:22 still says "highest priority first", which is now ambiguous (the highest *number* is the lowest priority). Proposed: line 28 uses `// "PZ"`, and line 22 reads "Open, unclaimed, unblocked; lowest `P` number first, then oldest; ...".

**5. Migration script: it relabels the `P?` issues.** #655, #658 and #659 carry `P?` beside a stray `P2`. Step 4 (`decisions/1189-p1-p9-scale.md:106-112`) has no `P?` guard. All three are `enhancement` without `effort:max`, so each one ends up `P?` + `P6`. That is an agent relabelling paused issues (AGENTS.md:122-129), and dropping the stray `P2` is the maintainer's call, which he is being asked about separately. Fix: at the top of steps 2, 3 and 4, add `if "P?" in n: print(f"#{i['number']}: P? - skipped, maintainer's"); continue`.

**6. Migration script: old-`P1` defects can land at `P5`, and the red-main `P2` branch can never fire.** Line 89 tests labels that do not exist: `gh label list` on the repo has no `blocked-main`, `red-gate` or `area:process`. So nothing ever becomes `P2`. Line 91 then sends *any* old `P1` with `area:build`/`area:mcp` to `P5` **before** the bug check. The red-main bugs this rule was written for (#1146 and #1184 are both `bug` + `area:build` + `P1`) would land at `P5`: below `P3`, and outside the cut blocker. Today this hits open #1021 (`bug`, `area:build`, `P1`) -> `P5`. A fork running the same script would mislabel its red-main issues the same way. Fix:
```python
P2_SET = set()   # red-main bugs, filled from the dry-run (like P4)
...
if "P1" not in n or "P?" in n: continue
bug = "enhancement" not in n
if bug and i["number"] in P2_SET:            new = "P2"
elif bug:                                    new = "P3"
elif "area:mcp" in n or "area:build" in n:   new = "P5"
elif i["number"] in P4:                      new = "P4"
else:                                        new = "P6"
```
Also make the dry-run print the old-`P1` bugs whose title starts "main is red"/"main red" as `P2` candidates.

**7. Migration script: the old-`P2` mapping does not match its own text.** Lines 110-111 send every old-`P2` enhancement without `effort:max` to `P6`. The decision file's Mapping (lines 29-30) and the issue's step 4 say "enhancements -> `P8` (`P6` where an open PR works them)". The script lifts the whole old-`P2` enhancement backlog above `P7` bug polish. Fix: `new = "P6" if "in-review" in n else "P8"` (`in-review` stands in for "an open PR works it"), or change the Mapping text if `P6` is what is meant. The text and the script must say the same thing.

**8. Migration script: it is unsafe to re-run after a partial failure.** `gh(..., check=True)` raises on the first failed edit, which leaves a half-migrated tracker. Suppose a re-run follows a failure in step 3 or 4. Its step 2 then sees the *new-meaning* `P1`s (the former `P0`s, e.g. #1174, a wrong-output issue) as old `P1` and moves them to `P3`. That demotes unsafe-output issues, which is the exact hazard the decision file's "Watch 1" names. Fix: a guard before step 1. If the `P0` label no longer exists, or any open issue already carries one of `P3`..`P9`, exit with "migration already started - finish by hand from the audit list". Also print the audit log as it goes (it already prints per move), so a crash leaves a record.

### Notes (not blocking)
- `--dry-run` is side-effect free: it only runs `gh label list` and `gh issue list`; every create, edit, move and delete sits behind `if not DRY`. It touches open issues only (`--state open`).
- `gh label delete P0` removes the label from **closed** issues too, so line 41 ("closed ones keep their history") is not quite true for `P0`. Re-describing `P1`/`P2` also changes what closed old-`P1` issues appear to mean. Consider keeping `P0` with the description "retired 2026-11-12: now `P1`" instead of deleting it.
- Nothing detects an issue that ends with two numbers (an issue carrying `P0`+`P1` or `P1`+`P2` gets two moves). None exist today (checked). A final pass that prints any open issue with more than one of `P1`..`P9` would make that visible. Relatedly, AGENTS.md has no rule for an issue found with two numbers (jq `first` picks one arbitrarily). Suggest: "report it to the maintainer; it is read by the lower number meanwhile".
- Old-`P1` issues with neither `bug` nor `enhancement` (bug lane by default) fall to `P3`, "defect", in the script. The dry-run reader should check those.
- "`P4` only where the maintainer asked ... the issue quotes them" (AGENTS.md:114-115) has no checker. The `classify-effort audit` or the `/review-prs` maintenance sweep could list `P4` issues with no quoted maintainer line.
- Neither gh-issues Pick snippet excludes `P?`, so paused issues show up in the "next" list as `PZ`. Adding `-label:\"P?\"` to both `--search` strings would match AGENTS.md:86.
- AGENTS.md:112: "only P1 and P2 block a release cut" is the question-dialog option, not words he typed. "(maintainer's choice, question dialog, 2026-11-12: ...)" would match how line 95's reading is sourced.
- The enhancement lane still puts any user-filed issue before agent-filed ones, so a user-filed `P9` is worked before an agent-filed `P4`. That is unchanged law; it is only noted here because the new scale makes it visible.
- Colours and descriptions are sensible (red/orange for the cut-blocking `P1`/`P2`, then fading). `P2`'s description says "blocks a cut" and `P1`'s does not, but both do; add "blocks a cut" to `P1` too.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

**Read, not built: text only.** No blockers left. This is a law change, so it waits for the maintainer's yes (`needs-maintainer`).

This is a re-check at head `0a1bdc3b` (main merged in, then `0a1bdc3b` on top). I read `git diff 5c8c32dc..0a1bdc3b` for the PR's own files and re-read AGENTS.md in full at the head. Against main (`50efdd39`) the PR changes only the 14 text files: no code, no `.github/`, no build script. `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` is 29 (main 28). No label or issue was changed by the PR.

### The eight earlier blockers: all closed
1. **One cut rule.** AGENTS.md:113-115 and :802-803 now say the same thing: no minor/major cut starts "while any `P1` or `P2` issue is open; a `P3` or lower never holds one". The decision file is fixed to match: line 13, and the dropped option at lines 24-26 now records the narrow reading as rejected.
2. **MCP rule.** AGENTS.md:519-524 now reads: owed agent-surface work (a tool, script verb or skill row for a shipped command) is `P5`, and "a defect in MCP code is rated by severity like any defect, `P1`-`P3`". The camcraft-mcp skill rows stay `P5` for the `MCP: <command>` follow-up, which is consistent.
3. **Untriaged issues.** AGENTS.md:90-91 ("untriaged, not lowest: it is triaged before any pick") and the new bullet at :122-127 cover it. I ran the new jq read-only against the live repo. It prints "TRIAGE THESE FIRST" with #72, #258, #361, #363, #435, #485, #836, then the numbered list. #655, #658 and #659 do not appear at all, because `-label:"P?"` drops them from the search. So a `P?`-only issue is never listed as untriaged.
4. **Snippets agree.** `claim-workflow.md:22-33` is now identical to `SKILL.md:52-59` (`// "!"`, "lowest `P` number first"). The pick-next-issue case.yaml and grader agree with each other and with the snippet.
5. **`P?` guard.** Decision file :132-136. Issues with `P?` are never given a number; a stray old number is planned as a removal (`new=None`, phase 4) and listed separately. The end assertion at :194 fails on any `P?` beside a number.
6. **Explicit buckets.** `--main-broken` and `--requested` (:78-79, :121) replace the guessed labels. The old-`P1` rule order is bug first (:145-146: `P2` only if listed, else `P3`), so a bug never lands in `P5`. Old-`P1` `area:build` bugs are printed as candidates (:150, :163-164).
7. **Old `P2` enhancements.** :154 maps them to `P8`, or `P6` only when an open PR closes or refs the issue. This matches the Mapping at :30-31.
8. **Re-runs.** The plan is derived once from the pre-migration labels (:112-168) and frozen in a file. Each applied row is recorded (:183-184), and a re-run skips applied rows (:179). With no plan file, the script refuses to start if any issue already carries `P3`..`P9` (:117-120). On re-run, "old" is read from the plan, never re-derived, so a former `P0` that is now `P1` can no longer be moved to `P3`. `--dry-run` exits at :170-172 before any label call or file write. The `P0` label is kept and re-described (:187), and the end assertion at :193 fails on any open `P0`.

### What the rework may have opened (notes, none blocking)
- **11 owed MCP issues would land in `P3`.** Old-`P1` issues with neither `bug` nor `enhancement` are planned as bugs (`P3`). Today those are exactly 11 issues: #1084, #1062, #1013, #962, #954, #937, #734, #732, #731, #730, #729. All are `area:mcp` and titled `MCP: ...`, which is owed agent-surface work: `P5` by the PR's own new MCP rule. As planned, they would sit in the fix-now `P3` band (11 of the 28 `P3`s) and be worked ahead of the maintainer's `P4` list. The error is upward, not a defect demoted, and the script lists them for a by-hand check, so it is not a blocker. I would change the line before running it: `elif "bug" not in n and "area:mcp" in n: new = "P5"`, placed before the `elif bug:` at :146. Or pass them by hand after the dry-run.
- **An issue filed mid-migration.** The real run plans and applies in the same process, so the window is seconds. A new `P0` filed in it stays `P0` and the end assertion fails loudly (good). A new old-style `P1` filed in it (by a session still on PROCESS_VERSION ≤28) would pass the assertion as a new-meaning `P1`. That is upward again, so it is safe, but invisible. A cheap guard is to print every open `P1` at the end that the plan did not produce from a `P0`. The dry-run and the real run also plan separately, so the real plan can differ from the list the maintainer read. Running the real pass right after the dry-run keeps that gap small.
- **Two old priorities.** No open issue carries two today (checked). If one appears, it is listed, left out of the plan, and the end assertion fails on it. That is loud, which is correct.
- **End assertion.** The 19 untriaged issues make the assertion exit 1 on every run until they are set by hand, so a real failure would show among expected lines. Consider printing the untriaged issues as their own list and asserting only on the rest.
- **`P0` description edit.** :187 assumes the `P0` label exists. A fork without one would stop there after all the moves (harmless, but noisy).
- **AGENTS.md, new tensions for the maintainer.** "User-reported bugs outrank owed work of the same number" (:89-90) is explicitly within a number, so the number wins. A user-reported bug is `P3` by the table ("wrong behaviour a user hits") unless it is polish, so it does not sink to `P7` unless whoever triages it rates it as polish. The enhancement lane still takes user-filed issues first, then the number, which means a user-filed `P9` is worked before an agent-filed `P4`. That is unchanged law, but the scale now makes it visible.
- **Stale PR body.** The body's "Rules changed" bullet still says "I kept the scope 'it opened'", and line 34 still mentions "guessed label names". Both are superseded by the rework section. Worth trimming, so the maintainer reads only the current rules.
- The skill's generic Pick snippet does not exclude `in-review` or `needs-research` (#258 and #361 show up under triage). AGENTS.md's own Pick search still does, and it wins.

### What the maintainer is agreeing to
- Priorities become `P1`..`P9`, lowest number first. `P1`-`P3` are defects only, and **any open `P1` or `P2` holds every minor/major cut**. Owed MCP and skill work is `P5`; follow-ups are `P7`; an issue with no priority is triaged before any pick. `P?` is unchanged, except that the stray `P2` is removed from #655, #658 and #659.
- After the merge, the migration script relabels today's open issues. These counts are my read-only recomputation of its plan from the live labels, with `--requested 530-548,617,661,1103,1104` and an empty `--main-broken`; the PR body gives no counts. Result: **P1 5, P2 0, P3 28 (11 of them the MCP issues above), P4 20, P5 14, P6 22, P7 20, P8 51, P? 5** (3 of them lose a stray `P2`). 19 untriaged issues are left for a hand pass.
- `P0` stays as a retired label on closed issues. The `P1`/`P2` label descriptions change, so closed old-`P1` issues will show the new meaning in their label tooltip.

**Conflict (found after posting):** GitHub now reports the PR CONFLICTING with main `50efdd39`. A local `git merge-tree` shows the only conflict is `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` (main 28 from #1194, this PR 29). Merge main into the branch and keep 29; nothing else conflicts. Labelled `conflicts` and turned back to draft until then. After that merge-of-main it goes back to `needs-maintainer` without a new review.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

After the clean re-check of 0a1bdc3b the branch took one small round, read by the main session: a merge of main (`.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` stays 29, main reads 28), the reviewer's one-line script fix (an old `P1` without `bug` that is `area:mcp` or titled `MCP:` plans as `P5`), and the PR body's counts. GitHub: MERGEABLE. Labelled `needs-maintainer`: a change of the Issue Law merges only on his yes; the relabel script in the decision file runs once right after the merge.
Maintainer (question dialog, 2026-11-12): "Yes, merge and relabel". Merging; the relabel runs next (dry run first).
